headline: Micron Leads Chip Rebound as Memory Shortage Talk Powers Friday's Rally
body_html:
Micron led a sharp rebound in chip stocks on Friday, rising 7.60% as investors returned to the memory names at the heart of the AI trade. The move helped lift the Nasdaq 2.69% and the S&P 500 1.62%. Semiconductors averaged a 4.77% gain, the strongest of any sector group.

Supply was the story. Coverage pointed to tight memory availability into 2027, and Micron's chief executive has said shortages could worsen in 2028, though research firm TrendForce expects prices to fall. That disagreement will keep the debate alive. Sandisk jumped 15.96%, while Tesla rose 5.22%, Broadcom 3.82% and TSMC 3.21%. NVIDIA lagged the group with a 0.80% gain.

Participation was wide: 564 stocks rose and 101 fell out of 665 tracked. Energy gained 2.38% and materials 2.04%. Markets reopen Monday, November 30, and the first test is whether the chip rebound holds. Investors will also watch NVIDIA chief Jensen Huang's Capitol Hill visit, and Micron's reported buyback window opening December 9.

briefs.headline: Memory and optical names top the leaderboard
briefs.body: Sandisk rose 15.96% and Coherent gained 14.07%, with Applied Optoelectronics up 10.48%. The gains show the rally reaching beyond the largest chipmakers into storage and optical networking, the parts of the AI build-out where the biggest percentage moves came on Friday.

briefs.headline: Tesla extends a standout week
briefs.body: Tesla rose 5.22% on Friday after what coverage described as its best week in 18 months. Reports cited a Cybercab fleet above 1,000 vehicles in Texas and a possible purchase of a German toolmaker, as the company pushes ahead with its Optimus plans.

briefs.headline: Broadcom gains as investors weigh a mixed AI picture
briefs.body: Broadcom rose 3.82%. Commentary was split between a report of a trimmed Google chip order and bullish forecasts that its AI revenue could roughly double in 2027. Its stake in Anthropic has also moved into positive territory, according to recent coverage.

briefs.headline: Few losers, and healthcare trails the field
briefs.body: Vertex Pharma fell 5.24%, Robert Half 3.98% and Wix.com 3.79%, the steepest declines in a session where only 101 of 665 stocks fell. Healthcare averaged a gain of just 0.67%, one of the weakest sector showings.

briefs.headline: Cyclicals join the advance, and London follows
briefs.body: Energy averaged 2.38% and materials 2.04%, so the rally was not confined to technology. Britain's FTSE 100 also posted its biggest weekly gain in eight months, led by miners and banks. Meanwhile, the Czech lower house approved a windfall tax on refineries that will hit Orlen.

briefs.headline: Iran blockade stays a risk to watch
briefs.body: The US disabled a ship trying to leave Iran, and Tehran vowed to confront the blockade. Friday's rally largely looked past the standoff, but energy stocks gained 2.38%, so any escalation could quickly return to the market's focus when trading resumes Monday.
